Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions on retention and deletion behavior. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

  - Confirm Redwood's SOC 2 status and provide a short summary (Neha will follow up).
  - Clarify how deletion SLAs apply to primary storage vs backups and what options we can offer for faster purge windows.

Hi Elena —

Thanks — happy to clarify. Short answers up front, followed by details.

- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (security + availability in scope) for our hosted and dedicated offerings. I've attached a 2-page SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). For customers who need the full report we can start an NDA-backed sharing process.

- HIPAA/GDPR: We support HIPAA-regulated workloads and can sign a BAA on request for Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted API customers we evaluate on a case-by-case basis and typically require Dedicated or Private for PHI. GDPR controls (data subject request processes, Data Processing Addendum) are available — we'll surface the DPA as part of contracting.

- Deletion SLAs (primary vs backups):
  - Primary storage: when a deletion request is executed (via API or console), records and associated artifacts are removed from primary storage within 24 hours in the default configuration. We can scope shorter windows (e.g., 4-6 hours) as a contractual SLA for Dedicated customers.
  - Backups & snapshots: we retain nightly backups and point-in-time snapshots for disaster recovery. By default, deleted records are not immediately purged from historical backups; backups are immutable for data integrity and recovery. Our default backup retention window is 90 days for log/operational backups and 180 days for full backups (configurable).
  - Backup deletion options: For customers requiring deletion-from-backups within a contractually defined timeframe we offer two options:
    1) On-request cryptographic shredding: we rotate and retire encryption keys that render the backup data unreadable; this provides an irreversible logical purge of the encrypted backup within a defined SLA (typically 30-90 days depending on snapshot lifecycle).
    2) Accelerated retention sweep: we can implement an accelerated backup lifecycle for your account that shortens backup retention periods and enforces earlier snapshot pruning (example: reduce snapshot retention to 30 days). This is best scoped for Dedicated or Private deployments.

- Logs: application and audit logs are retained by default for 90 days. If you require longer retention for e-discovery or audit purposes we can extend to 365 days or export logs to your tenant-managed storage.

- Evidence & questionnaire: We can complete Amaya's vendor questionnaire — for many questions we'll link to artifacts (SOC 2 summary, pen test summary, architecture diagram) and provide written responses. If helpful I can start filling your questionnaire; alternatively, we can provide answers in our security portal and share a read-only link.

Attached is a short retention matrix (data-retention-sla-table.xlsx) that maps default behavior to contractual options. A couple of notes you'll likely see in the table:
  - "Immediate delete" in primary does not guarantee removal from immutable backups unless a key-rotation or accelerated retention option is chosen.
  - For HIPAA customers we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments if you need strict backup purge SLAs.

Proposed next steps:
  1) Elena — please send your vendor questionnaire (or a link) and call out any non-negotiable retention windows.
  2) Marissa/Rishi/Neha — we'll prepare a 1-page response pack and proposed contractual language for backup purge SLAs and BAA if required.

Happy to jump on a short call with your InfoSec to walk through technical details.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha@redwoodinference.com
